input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 (second instance) binds us, the Customer, not the Vendor: it prohibits developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring any competing product or service for the term plus twenty-four months in any territory. The scope is undefined ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and the post-term tail exceeds 12 months, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, which records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." We therefore strike the restriction entirely, marking the section intentionally omitted; no affirmative re-grant is needed because retained Section 12.3 already confirms nothing restricts our products, fields, or territories. (The separate no-hire covenant in the first Section 12.4 is addressed under its own rule.)

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Strike the Section 12.4 non-compete restriction on Customer, leaving the section intentionally omitted
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products or businesses we may develop, sell, or acquire, so we have struck this non-compete, which also contradicted Section 12.3. If you need protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only and no longer than 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
